items.title: Subtitle Placement
items.summary: By keeping subtitles more prominent, we can significantly reduce misunderstandings in noisy environments and improve overall user satisfaction. Users will be able to follow conversations more easily, leading to better comprehension and reduced social friction.
items.probe: Define one fixed subtitle position rule for V1: keep subtitles at the bottom center of the display.

choices.label: More Prominent
choices.description: Bias toward easier visibility over subtlety.

items.title: Confidence Display
items.summary: A well-defined confidence display will help users trust the system more, leading to better engagement and utilization of the subtitles and memory support features. This improved trust can also reduce social friction by making the system seem less intrusive and more helpful.
items.probe: Choose one confidence display format for V1: label only or label plus short reason.

choices.label: Label Only
choices.description: Keep certainty display minimal and fast to parse.

choices.label: Label + Reason
choices.description: Expose a short reason to improve trust.

items.title: Memory/Cache Policy
items.summary: This approach will enhance memory recall accuracy and reliability by prioritizing recently seen entities, thus reducing the likelihood of outdated or irrelevant data affecting the wearer's understanding and responses in real-time interactions.
items.probe: Set one local cache eviction rule for face/name memory in V1.

choices.label: Smaller Cache
choices.description: Bias toward tighter local memory and lower load.

choices.label: Recency First
choices.description: Bias toward recent names and conversations.

items.title: Phone/Cloud Boundary
items.summary: By keeping subtitle processing local, we reduce battery drain from always-on sensors and heavy inference tasks, ensuring that subtitles are clear and stable in noisy environments. This enhances user trust and daily-use value without adding unnecessary complexity or latency.
items.probe: Choose one phone-local versus cloud fallback boundary for face/name recall lookup in V1.

choices.label: Phone First
choices.description: Keep critical work local unless clearly necessary.

choices.label: Balanced Fallback
choices.description: Allow cloud assist for slower or richer lookups.

items.title: Visual Hierarchy
items.summary: By defining this visual priority rule, we can ensure that the wearer's attention remains focused on critical information (subtitles) while still providing necessary contextual cues (one-line support). This balance enhances trust and usability without causing distraction.
items.probe: Define one visual priority rule between subtitles and one-line support in V1.

choices.label: Subtitles Dominate
choices.description: Keep subtitles above all other overlays.

choices.label: Balanced Overlay
choices.description: Allow prompts to share attention more evenly.
